item.title: The Climbing Finger — What the Evidence Says About Connective Tissue
item.description:
A study-based look at the connective tissue of the human finger — how the pulley system is built, how it responds to load, how it fails, and how it heals. Plus a closer look at pulley thickening after injury, and why damaged connective tissue often feels stiffest after rest rather than after loading.

  • Finger Flexor Pulley Injuries in Rock Climbers — Miro, vanSonnenberg, Sabb & Schöffl, 2021 (Wilderness & Environmental Medicine)
  • Lack of tissue renewal in human adult Achilles tendon is revealed by nuclear bomb 14C — Heinemeier et al., 2013 (PubMed)

item.title: Müde und trotzdem aufgedreht — das autonome Nervensystem
item.description:
Warum man erschöpft sein kann und trotzdem nicht runterkommt. Was Sympathikus und Parasympathikus wirklich tun, welche Dinge welchen Ast anschalten, warum Sport beruhigt und trotzdem dämpfen kann — und welche Hebel die Evidenz hergibt, jenseits der Vagus-Versprechen. Zwei Stimmen, nüchtern, ~18 Min (Audio auf Englisch).

Sources

  • Psychophysiological effects of slow-paced breathing at six cycles per minute (Psychophysiology, Laborde et al.)
  • Slow breathing for reducing stress: the effect of extending exhale (ScienceDirect)
  • A Practical Guide to Resonance Frequency Assessment for HRV Biofeedback (Frontiers in Neuroscience)
  • Cardiac Parasympathetic Reactivation Following Exercise: Implications for Training Prescription (Sports Medicine)
  • Longer exercise duration delays post-exercise recovery of cardiac parasympathetic indices (PubMed)
  • Training History, Cardiac Autonomic Recovery and Performance in Recreational Runners (PMC)
  • Stimulating the Vagus Nerve: Eight Methods Reviewed by Science
  • Neuromodulation Applied to Diseases: The Case of HRV Biofeedback (PMC)

item.title: Erschöpfung — eine Landkarte der müden Systeme
item.description:
„Müde" ist nicht ein Zustand, sondern eine ganze Familie. Ein systematischer Rundgang durch die Arten der Erschöpfung — muskulär, metabolisch, nervlich-autonom, mental und emotional: wie jede entsteht, woran man sie erkennt, und was gegen welche hilft. Nüchterne Doku, zwei Stimmen, ~24 Min (Audio auf Englisch).

Sources

  • Central Fatigue vs Peripheral Fatigue: Mechanisms (Biology Insights)
  • Physical exercise-induced fatigue: serotonergic and dopaminergic systems (PMC)

  • Overtraining Syndrome: A Practical Guide (PMC)
  • A clinical allostatic load index, burnout and cortisol (PubMed)
  • Physical vs Mental Fatigue: Key Differences (Walk-In Lab)

item.title: Koffein, entzaubert (Folge 3)
item.description:
Was Koffein wirklich tut, warum es bei seltenem Konsum am stärksten wirkt, wie die Gene entscheiden wer davon profitiert und wer nervös wird — und wo es den Schlaf untergräbt, der die Müdigkeit eigentlich beheben würde. Folge 3 der Mini-Serie, als sachliches Interview (Audio auf Englisch).

item.title: Metabolische Flexibilität — Wie der Körper den Brennstoff wechselt (Folge 2)

item.title: Health Insurance on a German Tax Return - And the Refund Puzzle That Worries People
item.description:
In Germany, your basic health and care insurance contributions are fully tax-deductible — so why do some people find they get a bigger refund by leaving them off the return? A short explainer on deductions versus credits, the tradesperson tax credit, and why the tax office usually fills the numbers back in anyway.

Sources

  • Kranken- und Pflegeversicherung als Vorsorgeaufwendungen (Lohnsteuer kompakt)

  • Übermittlung der Beiträge an das Finanzamt (Die Techniker)
  • Steuerbescheid ändern mit eDaten: Korrektur nach § 175b AO (Lohnsteuer kompakt)

item.title: Does Acupuncture Work - And How Would We Even Know?
item.description:
Millions swear by acupuncture and acupressure — but how do you scientifically test whether any alternative therapy actually works? Using acupuncture as the case study, we take the claims seriously, then walk through the traps that fool us — regression to the mean, the placebo effect, sham needles — and land on what the evidence honestly shows.

Sources

  • Acupuncture for Chronic Pain: Update of an Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis (Vickers et al., Journal of Pain 2018)
  • Acupuncture for preventing migraine attacks (Cochrane review)
  • PC6 (P6) acupoint stimulation for postoperative nausea and vomiting (Cochrane review)
  • Is the Placebo Powerless? An Analysis of Clinical Trials (Hróbjartsson & Gøtzsche, NEJM 2001)
  • Placebo effects are weak: regression to the mean is the main reason ineffective treatments appear to work (DC's Improbable Science)
  • Acupuncture: a 'needle in the haystack' or a 'theatrical placebo'? (Edzard Ernst)

item.title: How Data Actually Travels - Down a Wire, Through Glass, and Across Thin Air
item.description:
Everything digital is just ones and zeros — but a copper wire, a strand of glass, and the open air don't know what a number is. So how does a bit physically travel? This episode follows a single one and zero through all three media, and finds the one idea they secretly share.

Sources

  • Line Coding — Network Encyclopedia
  • Digital-to-Digital Conversion — GeeksforGeeks
  • How fiber optics work: total internal reflection — AFL
  • Fibre Optic vs Copper — FiberMall
  • Sending data over RF signals — NetworkAcademy.IO
  • Understanding Modern Digital Modulation Techniques — Electronic Design

item.title: How an RSS Feed Actually Works
item.description:
We just built a private podcast feed for this show — so what is RSS, really? A short explainer on the quietly resilient format behind every podcast: why a feed is just a text file, how the audio lives elsewhere, and why your app pulls new episodes rather than being pushed them.

Sources

item.title: How RAM Is Made - And Why It Suddenly Costs So Much
item.description:
Why has RAM roughly doubled in price? This episode unpacks how DRAM is actually manufactured — the 1T1C cell, the brutal capacitor-etching that defines memory fabrication — and contrasts it with logic chips at a foundry like TSMC. Then it follows the money into HBM and the AI build-out to explain the 2026 memory shortage.

Sources

  • Samsung warns of memory shortages driving industry-wide price surge in 2026 (Network World)
  • Samsung and SK hynix warn AI-driven memory shortages could last until 2027 (Tom's Hardware)
  • DRAM and NAND prices jump as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron tighten supply (Astute Group)
  • DRAM: Device Fabrication (Entegris)
  • Why DRAM is stuck in a 10nm trap (Blocks & Files)
  • Scaling the Memory Wall: The Rise and Roadmap of HBM (SemiAnalysis)
  • Why is HBM so Hard to Manufacture? (Vikram Sekar)
  • SK hynix Partners With TSMC to Strengthen HBM Leadership
